correctness.rationale: The midpoint split is a bijection to ordered pairs of nonnegative prefixes ending at h, giving conditional independence and normalization by the square of the ballot total. Removing completed primitive excursions gives the coefficient of C(x)^(h+j) for h>0 and of C(x)^(j+1) for h=0, where the midpoint contact is counted separately. The consecutive-index ratios of these coefficient rows are decreasing, and the ratios b_(h+2)(j)/b_h(j) decrease on common support, including the distinct formula at h=0. The higher rows have no new upper tail. An interval-supported log-concave mass sequence has a TP2 convolution kernel, so Cauchy–Binet permits replacing the two summands consecutively in likelihood-ratio order. The shift by one at h=0 increases its log-concave sum law in that order. The resulting law has support [0,n−h] for h>0 and [1,n−1] for h=0, ensuring distinct laws and strictly decreasing conditional means at consecutive feasible heights. The independent-copy covariance identity proves the nonpositive assertion for weakly increasing transforms and strict Cov(H,R)<0 for n≥2; n=1 is vacuous. The frozen slogan's 'negative covariance for all' is understood in the nonpositive sense of the actual statement (constants give zero). A separately written full-walk DP (python3 /workspace/review_evidence/reproduce.py 5) checked 610,521 integer minors over all height pairs through n=34 and all corresponding strict mean comparisons. The finite check does not prove the universal assertion.

value.rationale: This identifies a finite-size likelihood-ratio dependence between two different structural statistics (renewal at ground level and midpoint excursion height), not just their correlation or marginals. It supplies ordered regression for arbitrary increasing contact transforms and includes the nontrivial obligatory-contact boundary at zero midpoint. The natural exact result is useful without an asymptotic claim.
